rejectionChanges.reason: نحن normally represents a subject pronoun, but English US can occur in constructions translated with Arabic subject forms. Do not categorically reject on case alone; bare-entry construction remains unresolved.
لونغ is not an established MSA translation of the long property. Keep both directions disallowed; register remains uncertain and status becomes review under the revised register rule.
صديقي is my friend and can be natural when addressing someone as friend. Do not reject every possessive adaptation; this isolated sense needs confirmation.
ارت is a phonetic rendering/name, not a certified Arabic art concept. Withhold both directions while register remains unclassified.
بالفيديو can naturally occur where English VIDEO modifies a communication medium. Isolated use needs context, so rejection solely for a preposition is too strong.
نصوص is plural texts, but TEXT can denote written material collectively. Defer the collective sense instead of automatically rejecting number differences.
الاسعار has both a hamza issue and a plural reading; contextual price/prices usage needs review, not automatic morphological rejection.
ماتش points to match, not much. The semantic exclusion is clear even while its register classification remains uncertain.
الخدمات may realize collective service in context. Bare-entry number/collective use needs review rather than blanket rejection.
حو is a truncated fragment, not a certified MSA around equivalent. Keep both directions disallowed and retain register review.
ضرائب can express TAX in the collective taxation sense. English tax as a mass/activity term can naturally take an Arabic plural.
المراة has an orthographic defect; Arabic singular woman can denote women collectively in some constructions. Do not reject solely for singular/plural form, but do not approve the text yet.
ضريبي can be tax-related in an attributive construction or my tax as written. The intended reading is unresolved, not automatically invalid because it is adjectival.
العملاء can occur naturally for attributive English CUSTOMER, as in customer service. Keep construction review instead of absolute singular/plural rejection.
البيع is the natural selling-activity sense of SALES. English lexical plural and Arabic mass noun need not match in form.
التشكيلة is a standard lineup/composition term. PROFILE might have a specialized overlap but is not certified here; review the sense rather than make an unsupported categorical rejection.
بوينت is not a certified natural MSA point noun in this relationship. Keep both directions disallowed pending lexical/register evidence.
مان is not a certified Arabic man noun in this relationship; retain exclusion while register remains uncertain.

دق is standard Arabic knocking/pounding, not HOTEL. Register can be MSA while the relationship is semantically wrong.
